wiki_catalogs.name: Overview
wiki_catalogs.prompt: Create comprehensive content for this section focused on the overall project. Explain the purpose of the Tinkoff Invest ETF Balancer Bot as an automated portfolio rebalancing tool for Tinkoff Investment accounts. Describe its core value proposition: enabling users to maintain target ETF allocations through intelligent, rule-based trading strategies. Cover the architectural style (modular monolith in TypeScript), primary use cases (portfolio rebalancing, margin trading, expense tracking), and integration with the Tinkoff API via tinkoff-sdk-grpc-js. Include high-level diagrams illustrating system context and data flow from configuration input to order execution. Highlight key features such as multiple rebalancing modes, buy requires total marginal sell logic, minimum profit thresholds, and exchange closure behavior handling. Discuss prerequisites for usage including basic investing knowledge, JSON literacy, and command-line familiarity. Provide real-world examples of how users benefit from automation and risk management capabilities.

wiki_catalogs.name: Minimum Profit Threshold
wiki_catalogs.prompt: Develop detailed content for the minimum profit threshold feature. Explain the calculation logic used to determine when a position can be closed based on profitability thresholds, including how cost basis, fees, and market prices are factored into the decision. Document configuration options such as `minProfitThreshold` in the CONFIG.json schema and their impact on trading behavior. Provide concrete examples from the codebase showing how this logic is applied during rebalancing, particularly in margin trading scenarios. Describe integration with the margin calculator and order execution pipeline. Address common issues like floating-point precision errors in profit calculations and edge cases where positions remain open despite being unprofitable. Include performance considerations for frequent threshold checks across large portfolios.

wiki_catalogs.name: Portfolio Rebalancing Engine
wiki_catalogs.prompt: Create comprehensive content for the portfolio rebalancing engine. Explain its architecture as a strategy-driven system implemented in balancer/index.ts, where different rebalancing modes (manual, marketcap, aum, decorrelation) are selected based on configuration. Detail how desiredBuilder.ts computes target allocations using input strategies and current market data. Describe the role of diffCalculator.ts in determining position deltas and diffManager.ts in orchestrating optimal trade sequences while respecting constraints like order limits and exchange closure rules. Include sequence diagrams showing data flow from configuration load to order execution planning. Provide code examples demonstrating each rebalancing mode with sample CONFIG.json snippets. Address common issues such as imbalanced allocations after execution and edge cases in fractional lot calculations.

wiki_catalogs.name: Configuration Structure
wiki_catalogs.prompt: Develop detailed content for the CONFIG.json structure. Explain each top-level property including accounts, targets, rebalancingMode, marginSettings, and exchangeClosureBehavior. Document the schema requirements for account objects (brokerAccountType, id, name) and target allocations (ISINs with percentage weights). Provide annotated examples showing single and multi-account configurations. Detail how environment variables are interpolated within the configuration using ${VAR_NAME} syntax. Illustrate nested structures for advanced features like decorrelation mode and AUM-based rebalancing. Include validation rules enforced by configLoader.ts and common structural errors with troubleshooting guidance.

wiki_catalogs.name: Expense Tracking
wiki_catalogs.prompt: Develop detailed content for the expenseTracker module. Explain how it captures transaction costs, fees, and other portfolio-related expenses during rebalancing operations. Document its integration with the provider module to record real trading costs from executed orders. Describe the data structure used for storing expense records and how they are persisted across runs. Include examples of how users can retrieve and analyze cumulative expenses over time. Address configuration options for custom cost tracking, accuracy considerations, and reconciliation methods against actual broker statements. Highlight usage patterns in both dry-run and live execution modes.

wiki_catalogs.name: Manual Rebalancing Mode
wiki_catalogs.prompt: Develop detailed content for the manual rebalancing mode. Explain how users define fixed target percentages for each ETF in CONFIG.json and how desiredBuilder.ts uses these static allocations to compute desired positions regardless of market dynamics. Document the implementation in balancer/index.ts where the strategy is selected via config.mode = 'manual'. Provide a complete example configuration with buy/sell decisions generated from an imbalanced portfolio state. Illustrate how lot size constraints and instrument availability are handled during order planning. Address common issues such as inability to reach exact targets due to minimum lot sizes and strategies for mitigating drift over time.

wiki_catalogs.name: ETF Metrics Collection
wiki_catalogs.prompt: Develop detailed content for ETF metrics collection tools. Explain the implementation of etfCap.ts for fetching AUM, market capitalization, and weight distribution data from T-Capital website using puppeteer-based scraping. Document pollEtfMetrics.ts functionality for collecting time-series ETF performance metrics, including historical analysis, cross-metric correlation, and error handling during data collection. Describe configuration options, execution patterns (standalone vs. integrated), and integration with rebalancing decisions. Provide examples of scheduling via cron jobs, handling rate limits, and processing output data. Address common failures such as selector changes on target websites and network resilience strategies.

wiki_catalogs.name: Order Execution Lifecycle
wiki_catalogs.prompt: Develop detailed content for the order execution lifecycle. Explain how diffManager computes buy/sell differences and passes them to provider for execution. Document the state transitions of orders from creation to completion or failure, including pending, submitted, filled, rejected, and retried states. Include practical examples from provider-order-execution.test.ts demonstrating successful and failed order flows. Describe idempotency mechanisms using request IDs and how duplicate executions are prevented. Illustrate with a state diagram the full lifecycle including retry logic on transient failures. Address integration points with Tinkoff gRPC API and error code handling such as 'ORDER_NOT_FOUND' or 'LIMIT_ORDER_SIZE_EXCEEDED'.

wiki_catalogs.name: Manual Mode Configuration
wiki_catalogs.prompt: Develop detailed content for manual rebalancing mode configuration. Explain how users define fixed target percentages for each ETF in the portfolio using the 'target' field in CONFIG.json. Document how the balancer interprets these static allocations during desired portfolio calculation without external data dependencies. Provide a realistic example of a manual mode configuration with multiple ETFs and their respective targets. Detail validation logic in configLoader.ts that ensures target values are valid numbers between 0 and 1, and that they sum to 1. Address common misconfigurations such as invalid percentage ranges or non-existent instrument IDs, and provide resolution strategies. Highlight use cases where manual mode is most appropriate, such as simple portfolios with stable allocation preferences.

wiki_catalogs.name: Minimum Profit Threshold
wiki_catalogs.prompt: Develop detailed content for the minProfitThreshold configuration option. Explain how it prevents closing positions unless a minimum profit target is met, reducing unnecessary trading and tax implications. Document its integration with the diffCalculator and marginCalculator modules, including threshold validation rules and edge cases (e.g., partial fills, market volatility). Include examples from test scenarios such as min-profit-threshold-logic.test.ts and min-profit-threshold-validation.test.ts. Describe configuration syntax in CONFIG.json, default behavior, and interaction with dry-run modes. Address common issues like unexecuted sell orders and strategies for tuning thresholds based on portfolio size and risk tolerance.

wiki_catalogs.name: Installation and Setup
wiki_catalogs.prompt: Develop detailed content for installation and setup procedures. Explain prerequisites: Node.js/Bun runtime, Tinkoff API token generation, and environment setup. Provide step-by-step instructions for cloning the repository, installing dependencies using Bun or npm, and verifying the installation. Detail the process of creating a CONFIG.json file from CONFIG.example.json, emphasizing required fields like account IDs, target allocations, and API credentials. Include examples of setting environment variables for secure credential management. Document common pitfalls during setup (e.g., incorrect token permissions, malformed JSON) and their solutions. Address platform-specific considerations for macOS, Linux, and Windows. Reference debugging scripts like debug-configloader.ts to help validate configuration loading. Ensure clarity for beginners while providing technical depth for automation and CI/CD integration scenarios.

wiki_catalogs.name: Exchange Closure Behavior
wiki_catalogs.prompt: Develop detailed content for exchange closure behavior strategies. Explain the three modes: skip_iteration, force_orders, and dry_run, detailing how each affects bot operation during non-trading hours or market holidays. Document implementation specifics in the provider module for detecting market closure states via Tinkoff API responses and time-based rules. Describe how the balancer adjusts its workflow based on these settings, including order queuing, state persistence, and retry logic. Provide real-world examples from test files that simulate market closure scenarios. Address integration with margin trading decisions and risk management implications of delayed executions. Include troubleshooting guidance for misconfigured closure handling and performance impacts of polling frequency adjustments.

wiki_catalogs.name: Margin Trading Support
wiki_catalogs.prompt: Develop detailed content for margin trading functionality. Explain how marginCalculator.ts implements risk-aware position management by calculating available buying power and enforcing margin requirements. Document the applyMarginStrategy method's behavior with different configuration options ('keep', 'reduce', 'close') and fallback logic when strategy is undefined. Describe integration points with the core balancer where margin positions influence buy/sell decisions. Include practical examples showing how margin accounts behave under various market conditions and configuration settings. Address common pitfalls like insufficient collateral errors and unexpected position closures. Provide debugging guidance using logs from marginCalculator and test scenarios from src/__tests__/utils/marginCalculator-enhanced.test.ts.

wiki_catalogs.name: Rebalancing Modes Configuration
wiki_catalogs.prompt: Develop detailed content for configuring rebalancing modes. Thoroughly explain manual, marketcap, aum, and decorrelation modes including their specific configuration parameters and behavioral differences. Document required fields for each mode (e.g., marketCapUrl for marketcap mode, aumSource for aum mode). Explain how the balancer interprets these configurations during desired portfolio calculation. Provide realistic examples of each mode's configuration in CONFIG.json. Detail validation logic in configLoader.ts that ensures mode-specific requirements are met. Address common misconfigurations and their resolution strategies.

wiki_catalogs.name: Profit Calculation
wiki_catalogs.prompt: Develop detailed content for the profitCalculator module. Explain how it computes realized and unrealized gains by comparing current market values with historical purchase prices and quantities. Detail its reliance on accurate position data from the Tinkoff API and transaction logs from the balancer. Describe the methodology for handling partial sales, currency conversions, and dividend impacts if applicable. Document the output format of profit reports and how users can access performance metrics over various timeframes. Provide practical examples showing profit calculations before and after rebalancing. Address edge cases such as closed positions, margin trades, and exchange closure scenarios.

wiki_catalogs.name: Market Capitalization Rebalancing Mode
wiki_catalogs.prompt: Develop detailed content for the market capitalization rebalancing mode. Explain how this strategy dynamically adjusts ETF weights based on their relative market caps, implemented when config.mode = 'marketcap'. Detail how etfCap.ts fetches real-time market cap data from T-Capital website using puppeteer scraping, and how desiredBuilder.ts normalizes these values into allocation percentages. Describe caching mechanisms and error fallbacks when external data is unavailable. Provide a step-by-step example showing market cap input transformation into target allocations. Address performance considerations around polling frequency and integration resilience under network instability.

wiki_catalogs.name: News Analysis Tools
wiki_catalogs.prompt: Develop detailed content for news sentiment analysis utilities. Explain scrapeTbankNews.ts implementation using puppeteer to extract financial news articles from T-Bank platform, including article metadata and content parsing. Detail analyzeNews.ts logic for performing sentiment analysis on scraped news, covering preprocessing steps, keyword extraction, and scoring algorithms. Document input/output formats, dependency on external NLP models or rules, and integration points with trading signals. Include usage examples, performance considerations when running at scale, and mitigation strategies for inaccurate sentiment classification. Address ethical considerations and limitations of automated news interpretation in trading contexts.

wiki_catalogs.name: Error Handling and Retry Mechanisms
wiki_catalogs.prompt: Develop detailed content for error handling and retry logic in order execution. Explain how network resilience is achieved through exponential backoff and jitter in provider network retry logic. Document classification of errors into transient (e.g., network timeouts) vs. permanent (e.g., invalid token) and corresponding handling strategies. Use examples from provider-api-error-propagation.test.ts to show how gRPC status codes are mapped to application-level exceptions. Detail the retry configuration parameters like max attempts, timeout thresholds, and circuit breaker patterns if applicable. Provide troubleshooting guidance for common failure scenarios such as authentication errors, rate limiting, and market closure conditions. Include performance implications of retry policies and best practices for tuning them in production.

wiki_catalogs.name: MarketCap Mode Configuration
wiki_catalogs.prompt: Develop detailed content for market capitalization-based rebalancing mode. Explain how this mode dynamically adjusts ETF allocations based on real-time market capitalization data fetched from an external source via marketCapUrl. Document required configuration fields including 'mode': 'marketcap' and 'marketCapUrl', explaining acceptable URL formats and expected JSON response structure. Provide a complete example of marketcap mode configuration in CONFIG.json with a mock API endpoint. Detail how desiredBuilder.ts calculates proportional weights from market cap values and normalizes them into portfolio targets. Include validation rules in configLoader.ts that verify URL validity and proper schema. Address potential issues like API downtime, malformed responses, and rate limiting, with recommended mitigation strategies such as caching or fallback mechanisms.

wiki_catalogs.name: Buy Requires Total Marginal Sell
wiki_catalogs.prompt: Develop detailed content for the buyRequiresTotalMarginalSell functionality. Explain how this safety mechanism blocks new purchases unless sufficient marginal selling capacity exists, preventing unintended margin debt on non-margin instruments. Document its implementation in the desiredBuilder logic, including calculation of available margin and position limits. Illustrate workflow with real-world examples from buy-requires-total-marginal-sell-integration.test.ts and buyRequiresEdgeCases.test.ts. Cover configuration flags, error handling when constraints are violated, and recovery procedures. Discuss risk mitigation benefits and performance trade-offs during high-frequency rebalancing.

wiki_catalogs.name: Command Reference
wiki_catalogs.prompt: Create comprehensive API documentation for all CLI commands exposed in package.json scripts. For each command (start, accounts, config, etf-cap, poll:metrics, etc.), document invocation syntax, available flags (e.g., --list-accounts, --once, --dry-run), and their effects on program behavior. Explain the purpose and workflow of each command, including hidden/debug commands like test_balancer_logic or debug_tobuylots. Provide practical usage examples demonstrating typical command sequences. Clarify how commands interact with configuration files and external services. Include error conditions and exit codes where applicable. Link each command to its corresponding implementation logic in src/index.ts and related modules. Address security implications of certain commands that trigger actual trades versus read-only operations.

wiki_catalogs.name: Sequential Order Execution
wiki_catalogs.prompt: Develop detailed content for sequential order execution patterns. Explain the importance of maintaining execution order for portfolio integrity, especially when managing interdependent buy/sell operations in margin accounts. Detail the implementation in the balancer's execution phase, where orders are processed one-by-one with status verification between steps. Document error handling mechanisms for partial fills, rejections, and API rate limiting during sequence processing. Provide examples from integration tests that validate correct sequencing under various market conditions. Describe how this pattern interacts with dry-run mode and logging for auditability. Address performance trade-offs between safety of sequential processing versus speed of parallel execution, and provide optimization recommendations for high-frequency use cases.

wiki_catalogs.name: Buy Requires Total Marginal Sell
wiki_catalogs.prompt: Develop detailed content for the 'buy requires total marginal sell' mechanism. Explain its purpose in preventing new purchases unless all existing margin positions can be fully liquidated, implemented in buyRequiresTotalMarginalSell.ts. Describe how this safety feature interacts with the rebalancing engine to modify sell priorities and block buy orders when margin exposure exceeds thresholds. Document configuration parameters that control this behavior and their impact on trading strategy. Provide real-world scenarios where this prevents over-leveraging during market downturns. Include code examples showing input/output transformations in the utility function and reference test cases from buyRequiresEdgeCases.test.ts and buyRequiresIntegration.test.ts to illustrate expected behavior under stress conditions.

wiki_catalogs.name: Multi-Account Management
wiki_catalogs.prompt: Develop detailed content for multi-account configuration support. Explain how the accounts array in CONFIG.json enables management of multiple Tinkoff brokerage accounts. Document the account identifier system and how configurations are applied selectively using --account flag. Illustrate scenarios with mixed account types (e.g., brokerage vs. IRA). Detail how configuration inheritance and overrides work across accounts. Explain the role of configLoader.ts in resolving account-specific settings and validating account references. Provide examples showing complex multi-account setups with different rebalancing strategies per account.

wiki_catalogs.name: Daily Aggregation
wiki_catalogs.prompt: Develop detailed content for the dailyAggregator module. Explain its role in summarizing daily portfolio activity including executed trades, associated costs, and performance changes. Describe how it structures time-series data for long-term analysis and reporting. Document the aggregation logic, data retention policies, and storage mechanisms used to maintain historical records. Include examples of generated reports and how they can be used to evaluate strategy effectiveness. Address integration with external analytics tools, data export formats, and methods for validating data integrity. Discuss performance implications when processing large volumes of historical data.

wiki_catalogs.name: AUM-Based Rebalancing Mode
wiki_catalogs.prompt: Develop detailed content for the AUM-based rebalancing mode. Explain how this strategy allocates portfolio weight proportionally to each ETF's Assets Under Management (AUM), activated by config.mode = 'aum'. Detail how etfCap.ts extracts AUM figures from T-Capital web pages, handles currency conversion, and manages missing or stale data. Describe normalization logic in desiredBuilder.ts that converts raw AUM values into investable percentages. Include a practical example demonstrating AUM data ingestion and resulting trade recommendations. Discuss limitations such as delayed reporting cycles and potential concentration risks in rapidly growing ETFs.

wiki_catalogs.name: Configuration Management Tools
wiki_catalogs.prompt: Develop detailed content for configuration management utilities. Explain configManager.ts functionality for validating, normalizing, and exporting configuration files programmatically. Document its role in ensuring CONFIG.json schema compliance, handling environment variable overrides, and supporting multi-account setups. Describe public methods for reading, updating, and testing configurations, along with validation rules enforced (e.g., percentage bounds, required fields). Provide code examples demonstrating programmatic configuration updates, integration with CI/CD pipelines, and use in automated testing scenarios. Address error handling for invalid configurations and compatibility with different configuration modes (simple, comprehensive, ultimate).

wiki_catalogs.name: Sequential Execution and Dry-Run Mode
wiki_catalogs.prompt: Develop detailed content for sequential order execution and dry-run capabilities. Explain how orders are executed in sequence to prevent race conditions and maintain portfolio consistency, particularly when rebalancing multiple instruments. Describe the dry-run mode that simulates execution without placing real trades, used for testing and validation. Reference order-execution-sequences.test.ts to demonstrate test cases for correct sequencing and safety checks. Detail how dry-run output mimics real execution logs while skipping actual API calls. Discuss use cases for dry-run in configuration tuning and risk assessment. Highlight safeguards that prevent accidental live execution during debugging and how command-line flags like --dry-run control this behavior.

wiki_catalogs.name: AUM Mode Configuration
wiki_catalogs.prompt: Develop detailed content for AUM (Assets Under Management) based rebalancing mode. Explain how this mode uses T-Capital's AUM data to determine optimal ETF weightings, favoring funds with growing investor interest. Document required configuration parameters including 'mode': 'aum' and 'aumSource', detailing supported sources such as 'tcapital'. Provide a realistic configuration example showing AUM mode setup with proper instrument mappings. Describe how etfCap.ts scrapes AUM data from T-Capital's website and how desiredBuilder.ts converts these figures into normalized allocation percentages. Detail validation checks in configLoader.ts ensuring aumSource is properly specified and recognized. Address common challenges such as website structure changes affecting scraping, missing AUM data for certain ETFs, and delays in data updates, offering solutions like retry logic or alternative data sources.

wiki_catalogs.name: Exchange Closure Behavior
wiki_catalogs.prompt: Develop detailed content for exchangeClosureBehavior configurations: skip_iteration, force_orders, and dry_run. Explain how each mode alters bot behavior when markets are closed, including decision logic in the provider module. Document use cases for each setting—skip_iteration for conservative operation, force_orders for time-sensitive strategies, and dry_run for simulation purposes. Reference implementation details from market-closure-scenarios.test.ts and provider-network-resilience.test.ts. Include guidance on selecting appropriate modes based on trading strategy, risk profile, and account type. Address logging outputs and monitoring implications for each mode.

wiki_catalogs.name: Configuration Guide
wiki_catalogs.prompt: Develop detailed content for the configuration system. Thoroughly explain the structure and semantics of CONFIG.json, including top-level properties like accounts, targets, rebalancingMode, and margin settings. Document all supported rebalancing modes (manual, marketcap, aum, decorrelation) and their specific configuration requirements. Explain advanced options such as minProfitThreshold, buyRequiresTotalMarginalSell, and exchangeClosureBehavior. Illustrate how configuration drives different components (balancer, provider, tools). Include guidance on testing configurations using provided test fixtures and common validation errors with troubleshooting steps.

wiki_catalogs.name: Margin Trading Risk Management
wiki_catalogs.prompt: Develop detailed content for margin trading risk management features. Detail the role of the marginCalculator utility in assessing available buying power and determining optimal position sizes while respecting account constraints. Provide code examples showing how margin positions are identified, evaluated, and managed during rebalancing cycles. Address edge cases such as sudden volatility spikes or funding rate changes. Include best practices for configuring margin settings safely and monitoring key risk indicators through the bot's reporting tools.

wiki_catalogs.name: Order Execution Framework
wiki_catalogs.prompt: Create architectural documentation for the order execution framework. Describe how provider/index.ts abstracts Tinkoff Investment API interactions for placing buy/sell orders with proper error handling and retry logic. Explain the integration between diffManager and provider in translating calculated differences into actual trades, including sequential execution and dry-run capabilities. Document critical concerns like idempotency, rate limiting, network resilience, and error propagation from gRPC responses. Include state diagrams showing order lifecycle transitions and failure recovery paths. wiki_catalogs.name: Advanced Configuration Options
wiki_catalogs.prompt: Develop detailed content for advanced configuration options. Explain minProfitThreshold enforcement logic and its impact on position closing decisions. wiki_catalogs.name: Decorrelation Rebalancing Mode
wiki_catalogs.prompt: Develop detailed content for the decorrelation rebalancing mode. Explain how this advanced strategy minimizes portfolio volatility by reducing exposure to highly correlated assets, selected via config.mode = 'decorrelation'. Detail how pollEtfMetrics.ts collects historical price data to compute correlation matrices and how desiredBuilder.ts applies optimization algorithms to maximize diversification. Provide a worked example showing correlation matrix calculation and resulting allocation shifts. wiki_catalogs.name: Debugging and Testing Utilities
wiki_catalogs.prompt: Develop detailed content for debugging and testing utilities. Explain debugBalancer.ts for step-by-step inspection of rebalancing calculations, including diff computation and order generation. Document verifyBalancerFix.ts purpose in validating fixes to balancing logic against known test cases. wiki_catalogs.prompt: Develop detailed content on security practices for API token management in order execution. wiki_catalogs.prompt: Develop detailed content for decorrelation-based rebalancing mode. wiki_catalogs.prompt: Develop detailed content for margin trading parameters including leverage limits, position sizing rules, and risk thresholds. wiki_catalogs.name: Core Features

<blog>
# Tinkoff Invest ETF Balancer Bot: Comprehensive Project Analysis

## 1. Project Introduction

The Tinkoff Invest ETF Balancer Bot is an automated trading system designed to rebalance Exchange-Traded Fund (ETF) portfolios according to user-defined target allocations. The bot connects to the Tinkoff Investment API to monitor portfolio positions, calculate rebalancing requirements, and execute buy/sell orders automatically.

**Core Goals and Objectives:**
- Automate portfolio rebalancing for multiple ETFs across different accounts
- Support various rebalancing strategies based on market capitalization, AUM, or custom weights
- Implement margin trading capabilities with configurable risk parameters
- Provide detailed logging and reporting of trading activities and performance

**Target Audience:**
- Individual investors using Tinkoff Investment services
- Users seeking automated portfolio management for ETF holdings
- Technical users comfortable with JSON configuration and command-line tools

## 2. Technical Architecture

### Component Breakdown

The project follows a modular architecture with clear separation of concerns between components:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[Main Entry] --> B[Configuration Manager]
    A --> C[Provider]
    A --> D[Balancer]
    B --> E[Config Loader]
    C --> F[Market Data]
    C --> G[Order Execution]
    D --> H[Desired Wallet Builder]
    D --> I[Diff Calculator]
    J[Tools] --> K[ETF Metrics Poller]
    J --> L[AUM Calculator]
    J --> M[News Analyzer]
```

### Design Patterns

The application implements several key design patterns:

- **Singleton Pattern**: The `ConfigLoader` class ensures only one instance manages configuration data throughout the application lifecycle.
- **Strategy Pattern**: Different rebalancing modes (manual, marketcap, aum, decorrelation) are implemented as interchangeable strategies.
- **Dependency Injection**: Configuration and SDK instances are passed through function parameters rather than being globally accessed.
- **Event-Driven Architecture**: The main loop triggers balancing iterations at configured intervals.

### System Relationships

The core system relationships demonstrate how components interact:

```mermaid

    Main[src/index.ts] --> Provider[src/provider/index.ts]
    Provider --> ConfigLoader[src/configLoader.ts]
    Provider --> Balancer[src/balancer/index.ts]

    Provider --> ExpenseTracker[src/expenseTracker/index.ts]
    Provider --> ProfitCalculator[src/profitCalculator/index.ts]
    Provider --> DailyAggregator[src/dailyAggregator/index.ts]
```

### Data Flow

The data flow diagram illustrates the complete process from configuration to order execution:

```mermaid
flowchart TD

    B --> C[Fetch Current Portfolio]

    E --> F[Generate Buy/Sell Orders]
    F --> G[Execute Orders via Tinkoff API]
    G --> H[Track Expenses and Performance]
    H --> I[Log Results and Metrics]
```

## 3. Key Implementation

### Main Entry Points
- `src/index.ts`: Primary application entry point that orchestrates the balancing process
- `package.json`: Defines scripts for various operations including start, test, and tool execution

### Core Modules
- `src/balancer/index.ts`: Core logic for calculating position adjustments and executing trades
- `src/provider/index.ts`: Manages API interactions with Tinkoff Investment services
- `src/configLoader.ts`: Handles loading and validation of configuration files
- `src/balancer/desiredBuilder.ts`: Implements logic for determining target portfolio allocations

### Configuration Approach
- `CONFIG.example.json`: Template for the main configuration file with comprehensive comments
- Environment variables: Sensitive data like API tokens can be referenced via `${VARIABLE_NAME}` syntax
- Multiple account support: Single configuration file can manage multiple investment accounts

### External Dependencies
- `tinkoff-sdk-grpc-js`: Official Tinkoff Investment API client for market data and order execution
- `axios`: HTTP client for fetching external data (AUM, news, etc.)
- `puppeteer`: Browser automation for scraping financial data from web pages
- `lodash`: Utility functions for data manipulation and array operations

### Integration Points
- Tinkoff Investment API: Primary integration for portfolio data and trade execution
- T-Capital website: Scraping AUM (Asset Under Management) data for ETFs
- T-Bank news platform: Integration for retrieving fund-related news articles
- OpenRouter API: Potential integration for AI-powered analysis (referenced in environment setup)

## 4. Key Features

### Functionality Overview

The ETF Balancer Bot provides comprehensive portfolio management capabilities with several advanced features:

- **Multi-Account Management**: Support for managing multiple Tinkoff investment accounts from a single configuration
- **Flexible Rebalancing Strategies**: Multiple modes for determining target allocations including manual, market capitalization, AUM-based, and decorrelation strategies
- **Margin Trading Support**: Configurable margin trading with risk management parameters
- **Advanced Order Sequencing**: Intelligent ordering of trades to ensure proper fund availability
- **Comprehensive Monitoring**: Detailed logging, expense tracking, and performance reporting

### Implementation Highlights

#### Dynamic Configuration Loading
The `ConfigLoader` class provides robust configuration management with validation and environment variable integration:

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Idle
    Idle --> Loading: loadConfig()
    Loading --> Validating: validateConfig()
    Validating --> Ready: Success
    Validating --> Error: Invalid Configuration
    Error --> Idle: Retry/Exit
    Ready --> Using: getConfigValue()
    Using --> Idle: resetInstance()
```

#### Smart Rebalancing Logic
The balancer implements sophisticated logic for determining optimal trade sequences:

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Start
    Start --> CheckFrozen: filterFrozenAssets()
    CheckFrozen --> CalculateCurrent: calculatePortfolioShares()
    CalculateCurrent --> DetermineTarget: buildDesiredWalletWithDiff()
    DetermineTarget --> CalculateDifferences: diffCalculator()
    CalculateDifferences --> PlanOrders: generateOrdersSequential()
    PlanOrders --> Execute: postOrder()
    Execute --> Track: expenseTracker.addExpense()
    Track --> Complete: [*]
```

#### Market Condition Awareness
The system handles exchange closure scenarios with configurable behavior:

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> CheckStatus
    CheckStatus --> Open: isExchangeOpenNow()
    CheckStatus --> Closed: Exchange Closed
    Open --> Balance: Normal Operation
    Closed --> Skip: skip_iteration
    Closed --> Force: force_orders
    Closed --> DryRun: dry_run
    Balance --> Complete: [*]
    Force --> Complete: [*]
    DryRun --> Complete: [*]
```

#### Advanced Position Management
The system includes specialized handling for margin trading and profit threshold enforcement:

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> AnalyzePositions
    AnalyzePositions --> IdentifyMargin: identifyMarginPositions()
    IdentifyMargin --> ApplyStrategy: applyMarginStrategy()
    ApplyStrategy --> CheckProfit: calculatePositionProfit()
    CheckProfit --> ValidateThreshold: meets min_profit_percent
    ValidateThreshold --> AllowSell: meets threshold
    ValidateThreshold --> BlockSell: below threshold
    AllowSell --> PlanTrade: include in orders
    BlockSell --> Exclude: skip sell order
    PlanTrade --> Complete: [*]
```
